summary: Christiansted harbor light on St. Croix: the 1919 keeper's house is an unroofed ruin beside an active range light; a 1924 hurricane made the lamp shake and had to be taken down.

structures.note: One-story concrete keeper's house, formerly with a lantern at one end; unroofed and heavily damaged in a 2022 photo.
17 ft (5 m) square skeletal tower beside the house, carrying the active range light (USCG 3-32870).

access.note: Site open, tower closed (Rowlett). Reached by road but not easy to find.

events.note: Rowlett's directory: station established 1857. The March 1918 inspection says the date of first build is 'Not known'. Disputed.
Virgin Islands lighthouse work placed under the Lighthouse Service by executive order of July 20, 1917; care and maintenance formally transferred August 16, 1917.
Listed among lights established during fiscal 1918, in the Commissioner's table that notes the Virgin Islands transfer.
Lens lantern (5th order improved, two red screens) reported by October 1918; the March 1918 inspection records no lens apparatus.
Characteristic changed October 4, 1918, to fixed red.
Present one-story concrete keeper's house (Rowlett's date for the structure).
Hurricane of August 2, 1924: slight damage; roof sheets loosened, house leaked, top of the bridge broken up; the lamp shook violently and had to be taken down.
Rowlett's directory: inactive since 1931. The USLHS light lists carry a light for the place in 1935, 1943 and 2004. Disputed.

corrections.why: Rowlett's directory lists an active range light at this site under USCG 3-32870, the same number as this record's aton. The record's inactive status fits the 1919 keeper's house but not the light. The USLHS place record says Active Aid to Navigation: No, which conflicts with Rowlett; a human should check which is current.
Rowlett's 2022 photo shows the 1919 building unroofed and heavily damaged, and the directory says the battered ruins still stand.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Commissioner's reports (FY1918) and the 1924 Bulletin spell the name Fort Louisa Augusta; Rowlett and the USLHS place record use Fort Louise Augusta. The story uses the Commissioner spelling; the record name is unchanged.

notes_for_editor: (1) First built: Rowlett gives 1857 as the year the station was established; the March 1918 inspection gives 'Not known' for the first build and says the structure was old when the keeper of 17 years took charge. The story states both. No source read supports the 1857 date directly. (2) Deactivation: Rowlett says inactive since 1931, but the USLHS light lists carry a flashing white light for this place in 1927, 1935 and 1943 and a 'Q W' light in 2004, and Rowlett describes an active range light (USCG 3-32870, the record's own aton number). The record's deactivated 1931 and status inactive are therefore disputed; see corrections. Rowlett calls the range light green; the light lists say white. The record lists 'Active Aid to Navigation: No' (USLHS place record). (3) Rowlett also says the original light 'was shown from a mast on the fort'; this conflicts with the 1918 inspection, which describes a lantern on a dwelling roof, and is not used. (4) Keepers: the 1918 keeper of 17 years is unnamed in the inspection extract; the October 1918 report says 'laborer in charge'. Philip A. Molley (USLHS roster, at least 1921) and R. A. Edwards (newspaper notice, August-September 1924) are not linked; no source shows whether they overlapped or followed one another. Molley's stint is the archive's own line, so the person slug is set. (5) Storm: the Bulletin's 'On August 2' is in the Sept 1, 1924 issue; the year 1924 follows from the issue. The OCR has 'St Croll: Island' and 'brIdge', 'brOken', 'vIolently', 'aved'; quotes copy the OCR exactly. (6) Chronicling America 'Fort Louisa Augusta' 1917-1940 returned 16 pages; the ten listed in the first search were all St. Croix Avis 1924 notices and advertisements, and the other six were not opened. One page was read in full for the notice. Nothing read in the newspaper adds to the hurricane description. (7) Commissioner FY1919 estimate for four 'unwatched' gas lights and five buoys in the Virgin Islands is not tied to this station and is not used. (8) The 1918 inspection coordinates (17 deg 45 min 31 sec N, 64 deg 41 min 49 sec W) differ from the record by about 0.4 km. No correction is proposed, because the inspection gives positions only to the arc-minute and no source read gives a better one. (9) Not read: the USCG Historian's page (history.uscg.mil, Article 1926607), which search showed as 'Built in 1919, inactive since 1931'. No archived capture was found (web.archive.org years 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 tried; live site returned 403). The snippet is not cited. (10) The St. Thomas Source article on the fort (2021) returned 403 and was not read. (11) Other stations of the same name are not used. (12) Fact-check 2026-10-28: every evidence quote was found in its cached source. The 1917 Commissioner paragraph is cited to pp. 6-7 because the quoted phrase falls on p. 6 and the placement on p. 7. (13) The roster line (Molley, 'at least 1921-') is matched to this record by name and state only: the place record has no position, and the roster is the archive's own line for this place. (14) The 1924 Bulletin's OCR reads 'brIdge' and 'brOken' in 'the top of the bridge was completely broken up'; the story reads 'bridge' and 'broken up' from the OCR and has not checked the page image. (15) Characteristic: facts.light.characteristic 'Q G' follows Rowlett's current range light (quick-flashing green); the USLHS 2004 entry under the same number (USCG 3-32870) reads 'Q W' (quick white). The story states the disagreement; a human should choose which value the light-at-night feature uses. (16) The FY1918 Commissioner table (p. 30) lists the station under 'Lights established during the fiscal year 1918' with no description; the story says so and does not infer what was established. (17) The March 1918 inspection gives the means of reaching the light as a boat (one mile from Christiansted); Rowlett's 2026 entry says the site is accessible by road. The story gives both without choosing. (18) Commissioner FY1918 p. 30: the transfer note is printed under the same table; the story attributes it to the note, not to the table's list.
